report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a professional culinary assistant, with a strong emphasis on baking/pastry (cakes), recipes, and chef-level cooking guidance.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens overwhelmingly shift toward culinary vocabulary across layers and positions:
  - Mid layers: “culinary”, “Food”, “Kitchen”, “Restaurant”, “Chef”, “Cooking”, “Café”.
  - Deep layers (20–25): dominated by pastry/baking terms — “Cake”, “baking”, “Baked”, “Bake”, “Baker”, “cakes”, “Butter”, plus domain markers like “Mediterranean”, “molecular”.
  - Persona/credential markers recur at pos0 across many layers: “Professional”, “Advanced”, “Master”, “Institute”, suggesting an expert/professional tone.
- The difference-norm concentrates heavily in later layers (esp. layer 25 pos0 is by far the largest), indicating a strong, global steering signal that biases continuations toward this domain from the start of generation.
- Consistency across positions 1–4 (with “culinary”, “Kitchen”, “Chef”, “baking”) shows the domain bias pervades the whole local context, not just a single token.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a professional culinary/baking behavior—Model B is specialized to produce recipes, cooking instructions, and chef-style advice, particularly in pastry/cakes.
